entry.title: fix: vocabularyBox appendReading writes to state.reading (closes #62)
entry.content:
fix: vocabularyBox appendReading writes to state.reading (closes #62)

The appendReading mutation wrote `state.appendReading += value` — a stray,
undeclared property — instead of `state.reading`, the field consumed by the
vocabulary box save path (VocabularyBox.vue: _reading -> this.reading ->
saved `reading`). So when multiple words were selected into a phrase, the
per-word readings appended by TextBlockGroup.vue never reached state.reading.
This matches the sibling mutations (appendSearchField -> state.searchField).

Impact is limited to reading-bearing languages (e.g. Japanese furigana) when
building a phrase; a no-op for languages without readings.

Adds tests/js/VocabularyBoxAppendReadingMutation.test.mjs (node --test, 3 cases):
accumulation onto state.reading, no stray property, sibling parity.

Note: the mutation correctness is verified deterministically by unit test +
frontend build. The end-to-end reader visual (a phrase reading rendering in the
vocabulary box) only manifests with reading-language content, which this
English-only test environment (no Japanese tokenizer) cannot produce; that
visual step is env-gated, but the fix itself is proven at the unit level.

entry.title: fix: fail-soft dictionary import progress broadcasts (EP-10)
entry.content:
fix: fail-soft dictionary import progress broadcasts (EP-10)

DictionaryImportProgressedEvent is a ShouldBroadcastNow event dispatched
synchronously inside the dictionary import HTTP request. With the default
broadcast driver (pusher) unconfigured or unreachable, the bare event() calls in
DictionaryImportService threw BroadcastException synchronously and aborted the
import mid-file — proven via a runtime experiment (BroadcastException: Pusher
error cURL 7 on a dead endpoint).

The equivalent chapter broadcasts (ChapterService, ProcessChapter) already guard
their ShouldBroadcastNow dispatches with try/catch; only the dictionary import
progress broadcasts were unprotected. Route all six progress dispatches through a
broadcastImportProgress() helper that keeps the synchronous broadcast but catches
\Throwable and logs a warning, so an optional broadcast backend can never abort a
dictionary import. No change to import logic, transactions, or any review/FSRS
data path.

Tests: DictionaryImportBroadcastFailSoftTest — guard swallows a throwing backend
and logs; control proves a raw dispatch on the same backend still propagates.

The FSRS scheduling-state label was re-implemented on five surfaces and had

route all five surfaces through it:
- Home/Statistics.vue (was 复习/重学 -> now 复习中/重新学习)
- Text/WordSensesList.vue (was review->学习中 -> now review->复习中)

Display-only: fsrs_state data, FSRS scheduling, ReviewCard and ReviewLog are
untouched. Lifecycle state (active/buried/suspended/archived) is a separate
concept and keeps its existing owner (ReviewCardLifecyclePresentation.js).

entry.title: fix: store review_cards fsrs datetimes as DATETIME not TIMESTAMP (clo…
entry.content:
fix: store review_cards fsrs datetimes as DATETIME not TIMESTAMP (closes #57)

review_cards.fsrs_due_at / fsrs_last_reviewed_at were MySQL TIMESTAMP (range
ends 2038-01-19). FSRS schedules a card's next due date up to
maximum_interval_days (default and clamp ceiling 36500 days ≈ 100 years, per
ReviewSettingsPresetConfig), so a maturing card's fsrs_due_at legitimately
exceeds 2038 and then fails to persist ("Incorrect datetime value"), aborting
the sole rating write path (ReviewCardService::recordReview → FsrsScheduling).
2099 in the AI-study-card tests is within this real range, not a test-only
sentinel — so the schema, not the test, is wrong.

Additive, idempotent migration widens both columns to DATETIME (range to year
9999), converging fresh builds and long-running installs alike. APP_TIMEZONE is
UTC with no per-connection time_zone override, so existing <=2038 values convert
without a shift. Only the storable range changes — no FSRS math, ReviewLog,
ReviewCard lifecycle, scheduling, or due semantics are touched.

Verified on isolated MySQL 8.0: fresh build yields DATETIME for both columns; a
year-2125 due date round-trips through the model; the previously-erroring
AiStudyCardPendingItemTest::test_generate_cards_does_not_reschedule_existing_fsrs_cards
now passes; ReviewFsrsTest + FsrsSchedulingServiceTest 76/76; new
ReviewCardDueDateRangeTest 2/2.

Closes #57.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat: per-run disposable test database runner (closes #55)
entry.content:
feat: per-run disposable test database runner (closes #55)

Stage C completes the #55 isolation. Stage A added a fail-closed guard that
refuses destructive schema resets on non-disposable databases; this makes the
safe path automatic so destructive-reset suites can *only* ever run against a
throwaway database.

On a testing run, tests/bootstrap.php now provisions a unique, process-owned
disposable MySQL database (linguacafe_disposable_<ts>_<rand>), repoints the
connection env at it plus the LINGUACAFE_DISPOSABLE_DB ownership marker (which
the guard authorises), and drops it on shutdown. A shared / long-lived /
recovery / dev / prod database is never connected to, so its migration ledger
and sentinel cannot be touched.

- new Tests\Support\DisposableTestDatabase: create / activate / drop; only ever
  drops databases this run created that still match the disposable-name
  contract (reuses DisposableTestDatabaseGuard::matchesDisposablePattern)
- DisposableTestDatabaseGuard: extract matchesDisposablePattern() for reuse
- tests/bootstrap.php: auto-provision + shutdown cleanup (no-op + fail-closed
  when no server connection is configured)
- tests: name uniqueness; drop refuses protected/shared/recovery and
  not-created-by-this-run names; real create/drop roundtrip; and the suite
  itself runs against an owned disposable DB

Verified on isolated MySQL 8.0: runner test 5/5; RefreshDatabase suites run
end-to-end on the disposable DB; the per-run database is created and dropped
with no leak; Stage A guard (12/12) and #54 regression (2/2) still pass. No
change to FSRS/ReviewCard/WordSense/ReviewLog, business logic, .env, or
AGENTS.md.

Closes #55.

entry.title: fix: bound composite-unique index columns so clean MySQL build succee…
entry.content:
fix: bound composite-unique index columns so clean MySQL build succeeds (#54)

A clean utf8mb4 MySQL build failed because composite unique indexes spanned
default VARCHAR(255) columns whose combined key length exceeded InnoDB's
3072-byte limit ("Specified key was too long"). Two create migrations drifted
wider than the canonical long-running schema:

- ai_study_card_pending_items: language_id -> VARCHAR(64), status -> VARCHAR(32)
  (canonical bounds recorded in #54 from the verified backup). Index drops from
  ~3080 to ~1424 bytes.
- reading_inline_sense_confirmations: language -> VARCHAR(64) (same canonical
  bound applied to a language identifier); surface/lemma word forms stay 255.
  Index drops from ~3088 to ~2324 bytes.

Full-value unique constraints are preserved (columns only narrowed, not
prefix-indexed). Word-form columns (normalized_word, surface, lemma) keep 255.
Editing the create migrations is the only possible fix: migrate:fresh aborts at
the CREATE before any later ALTER could run. Existing databases already carry
the bounded widths, so they are unaffected (no additive migration needed).

Verified: full migration chain now builds from zero on a fresh disposable
utf8mb4 MySQL 8.0 (53 tables); new FreshSchemaIndexLengthTest asserts the
bounded widths and that both unique indexes fit within 3072 bytes.

No change to FSRS, ReviewCard, WordSense, ReviewLog, business logic, .env, or
AGENTS.md. Closes #54.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix: fail-closed guard against destructive schema resets on shared te…
entry.content:
fix: fail-closed guard against destructive schema resets on shared test DBs

Source #55 (stage A) minimal containment. A RefreshDatabase-style
migrate:fresh accidentally pointed at a shared/long-lived testing database
can reset its schema and destroy acceptance state. This adds a fail-closed
guard that, while APP_ENV=testing, refuses destructive schema-reset
operations (migrate:fresh/refresh/reset, db:wipe, and any DROP/TRUNCATE DDL)
unless the target database is a unique per-run, process-owned disposable
database (name matching linguacafe_disposable_<run>_<id> and equal to the
LINGUACAFE_DISPOSABLE_DB ownership marker).

- new App\Services\DisposableTestDatabaseGuard (command + query decisions)
- AppServiceProvider: CommandStarting listener (CLI path) + testing-only
  beforeExecuting backstop (reliable for programmatic Kernel::call, fires
  before the first drop) mirroring the existing RestoreWriteFence pattern
- focused tests cover: no marker -> reject, shared/recovery/contains-"test"
  names -> reject, disposable-without-matching-marker -> reject,
  owned disposable -> allow, destructive-query classification, and that the
  connection-layer guard fires before any drop

Shared/recovery/dev/prod databases are never reset. Does not change .env,
AGENTS.md, schema, or any frozen product semantics. Refs #55.
